channel.title: BulkStem updates
channel.description: Signed BulkStem releases for macOS. Entries are added by the release pipeline.

item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description:
• In-app updates: «Check for Updates…» in the BulkStem menu. On the second launch BulkStem asks once whether to check for updates every day; when a new version exists, a window shows what changed, and it installs only when you press «Install Update». Nothing installs by itself.
  • Voyage Plan: a sea leg that crosses an ECA, a load-line area or another zone shows «N marks» and a small arrow; click the arrow to see the crossings under the leg — the mile, the time from the leg start, the arrival time and the fuel on board at each one, in the same words as the report. Voyage → Expand All Marks / Collapse All Marks.
  • A small sign before a leg's distance tells where the figure comes from (a BulkStem route, an imported ECDIS route, or your own figure kept beside a route); hover it for the details.
  • Inspector of a sea leg: the route the leg follows, «Use route estimate» (or «Use import distance») and «Detach route»; «Zones on this leg» with the ECA miles and, where the leg leaves the recorded load-line areas, the note on the Load Line Convention's Summer Zones; for each ECA entry the compliance method and the fuel changeover the calculation made (with several fuel systems, their common start, the thermal stage and when each one meets the limit), and at an exit from a compliant-fuel stretch into a looser limit «Set up change-back…» with your duration (1.0 h offered, editable); a «Reason» for the extra consumption; «Stretches» under «Where the numbers come from», with the sea margin when the voyage has one.
  • Routes, a new section in the sidebar: every route of the voyage — BulkStem's own estimates and the routes imported from the ECDIS — in one list with the distance, the difference from your reference figure (CVoyager, the voyage orders), the ECA miles, the passages and the legs each one feeds. Open a route for its summary, the zone crossings with the ETA at each, the legs, the miles per zone and the passages. «Use in Plan…» puts it on a sea leg — keep your typed distance or take the route's — and shows what will change before anything changes; one ⌘Z undoes it.
  • «New Route»: find the two ports by name or LOCODE, choose the berth, the pilot station, the anchorage or the locality, the passages to avoid (Suez, Panama, Kiel), the planning date and the loading condition; BulkStem plans the route on its own route data, without the internet, and keeps it in the voyage file. «Recompute» plans it again after you change an end, the passages or the date.
  • «Import File…» (also File → Import Route…, ⇧⌘I): choose a route file exported from the ECDIS; BulkStem reads it without the internet, finds the ports at its ends and stops, measures each leg on the WGS-84 ellipsoid and finds the zone crossings, then shows the import sheet, where you choose the plan legs that receive it. CVoyager RTE files are read in this build; RTZ, GPX, KML and CSV files are recognised and declined by name; BulkStem cannot read them yet. A file BulkStem cannot read is declined with the reason, and nothing changes.
  • The leg inspector's route link opens the route in the Routes section.
  • Settings → Route Data: the route data installed, what each set holds, its signature and its licences.
  • Initial Conditions → Consumption: two more groups of rates per profile — «At 0.50 % S» (ships with a scrubber) and «At 0.10 % S (ECA)» — used on a sea leg inside such an area while the ship is on compliant fuel; an empty cell means not entered, and the leg then uses the ordinary rates and says so. Right-click a profile to clear a group.
  • Vessel: the passport in two columns, with the file buttons in the heading — the compliance method in sulphur areas, the load-line marks to the millimetre with their displacements and the basis of the drafts (nothing preselected), the load-line length L, the dimensions and build dates, the NOx tier, the basis of the hydrostatic table and the keel thickness, the kind and sulphur of each fuel grade, the fuel systems for the changeover, and the holds. Margins & reserves gains «In ECA (SMS)», the reserve the compliant-fuel check reads inside the areas.
  • Initial Conditions → «ECA fuel», a new tab: is there enough compliant fuel for each area — what is needed and why, what is on board, SUFFICIENT or SHORT BY with «add it to the bunker stem»; the fuel burnt in the sulphur-limit areas with each changeover's window; and every fuel changeover of the voyage in order, with «Set up change-back…» at the exits.
  • Cargo Intake: the load-line zone boundaries along the laden legs are checked automatically — untick one to leave it out, «Edit…» to make it your own point; a checkpoint anywhere on a leg with its season or «by the zone»; «Cargo on board», the smallest margin to the load-line marks with a red «EXCEEDED — LOAD LINE WARNING», the points along the voyage and the points that could not be checked, with what to do about them.
  • The ECA fuel tab and the cargo screen show exactly the figures and the words of the bunker calculation report: the fuel needed for a compliant-fuel stretch and its shortfall add up from the parts shown, as on paper.
  • Report: the zone crossings under each leg; REGULATORY ROUTE SUMMARY with the load-line crossings and their cargo figures, the ECA and sulphur-limit crossings with the changeover times, the NOx Tier III areas, the fuel rules at berth and the manual consumption adjustments; a DWT calculation at a load-line zone boundary, a season change or a checkpoint; «Manual additions» in the summary.
  • Where a leg passes through a seasonal or tropical load-line area whose boundaries BulkStem cannot draw yet, a note names the area, also when both ends of the leg lie outside it (Yantai → Singapore through the China Sea area).
  • Engine 0.7.0. A file saved by 0.3.0 with zones does not open in 0.2.x: keep copies while you test. Files of 0.2.1 open as before and their fuel, time and maximum-cargo figures do not change; the one exception is the target-quantity mode, where a point without a draft limit is now checked against the summer mark.
